fullPassage: Stanford psychology professor Dr. Carol Dweck is the internationally recognized pioneer of the concept of "growth mindset" as a way to continually grow, learn, and persevere in our efforts. Dweck found that kids who are told they're "smart" actually underperform in future tasks, by choosing easier tasks to avoid evidence that they are not smart, which Dweck calls having a "fixed mindset." In contrast, Dweck found, kids who are praised not for their smarts but for their effort develop what Dweck calls a "growth mindset." They learn that their effort is what led to their success, and if they continue to try, over time they'll improve and achieve more things. These kids end up taking on tougher things, and feel better about themselves. "Emphasizing effort gives a child a variable that they can control," Dweck has explained.

✅ ② (A) 찾았다 — (B) 알아냈다/발견했다: (A)는 'found my lost keys(잃어버린 열쇠를 찾았다)'에서 찾다, (B)는 'Dweck found that kids...(연구로 알아냈다)'에서 알아내다/발견하다라는 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 세웠다: (A)는 '세우다'가 아닌 '찾다'
❌ ④ (B) 설립했다: (B)는 '설립하다(found-founded)'가 아닌 '알아내다(find-found)'
det.tip: found: ① find의 과거 '찾았다/알아냈다' ② found(설립하다)의 현재형과 구별

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a set of attitudes or beliefs that shape how a person thinks and behaves"

det.korean: mindset=사고방식: 사람이 생각하고 행동하는 방식을 형성하는 태도·신념의 집합
det.analysis:
❌ ① evidence: '증거'는 태도·신념의 집합이 아님
❌ ② variable: '변수'는 바뀌는 요인으로 사고방식이 아님
❌ ③ effort: '노력'은 행위이지 태도의 집합이 아님
✅ ④ mindset: '사고방식'은 사람의 사고·행동을 형성하는 태도·신념의 집합으로 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: mindset = 사고방식. attitudes or beliefs that shape thinking가 핵심

questions.passage: Dweck found that kids who are __________ (tell) they're "smart" actually underperform in future tasks. In contrast, Dweck found, kids who are praised not for their smarts but for their effort develop what Dweck calls a "growth mindset."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 과거분사 수동태: kids who are told (듣는 대상)
det.analysis: 'kids who are __________ (tell)'에서 아이들이 '듣는' 대상이므로 수동태(be + 과거분사)가 필요하다. tell의 과거분사는 told. tell → told → told.
det.tip: 수동태 be + 과거분사. are told = 듣다(수동). tell-told-told

questions.passage: In contrast, Dweck found, kids who are __________ (praise) not for their smarts but for their effort develop what Dweck calls a "growth mindset." They learn that their effort is what led to their success, and if they continue to try, over time they'll improve and achieve more things.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 과거분사 수동태: kids who are praised (칭찬받는 대상)
det.analysis: 'kids who are __________ (praise)'에서 아이들이 '칭찬받는' 대상이므로 수동태(be + 과거분사). praise의 과거분사는 praised. praise → praised. not A but B(A가 아니라 B) 구문과 함께 쓰임.
det.tip: 수동태 be + 과거분사. are praised = 칭찬받다. not for A but for B

questions.passage: Stanford psychology professor Dr. Carol Dweck is the internationally recognized pioneer of the concept of "growth mindset" as a way to continually grow, learn, and persevere in our efforts. Dweck found that kids who are told they're "smart" actually underperform in future tasks, by choosing easier tasks to avoid evidence that they are not smart, which Dweck calls having a "fixed mindset." In contrast, Dweck found, kids who are praised not for their smarts but for their effort develop what Dweck calls a "growth mindset." They learn that their effort is what led to their success, and if they continue to try, over time they'll improve and achieve more things. These kids end up __________, and feel better about themselves. "Emphasizing effort gives a child a variable that they can control," Dweck has explained.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: taking on tougher things=더 힘든 일에 도전하는 것 — 노력을 칭찬받은 아이들의 결과
det.analysis:
✅ ① taking on tougher things: 원문 일치. 노력을 칭찬받은 아이들은 결국 더 힘든 일에 도전하고 스스로에 대해 더 좋게 느낀다 ←정답
❌ ② giving up far more quickly: '더 빨리 포기'는 성장형 사고와 반대
❌ ③ avoiding all difficult work: '어려운 일을 피함'은 고정형 사고에 해당
❌ ④ ignoring their own effort: '노력을 무시함'은 노력을 중시하는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: These kids end up taking on tougher things

questions.passage: Stanford psychology professor Dr. Carol Dweck is the internationally recognized pioneer of the concept of "growth mindset" as a way to continually grow, learn, and persevere in our efforts. Dweck found that kids who are told they're "smart" actually underperform in future tasks, by choosing easier tasks to avoid evidence that they are not smart, which Dweck calls having a "fixed mindset." In contrast, Dweck found, kids who are praised not for their smarts but for their effort develop what Dweck calls a "growth mindset." They learn that their effort is what led to their success, and if they continue to try, over time they'll improve and achieve more things. These kids end up taking on tougher things, and feel better about themselves. "Emphasizing effort gives a child __________," Dweck has explained.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: a variable that they can control=통제할 수 있는 변수 — 노력 강조가 아이에게 주는 것
det.analysis:
❌ ① a reason to avoid every hard task(어려운 과제를 피할 이유): 노력 강조의 취지와 반대
❌ ② an excuse for their poor results(저조한 결과에 대한 변명): 본문 근거 없음
✅ ③ a variable that they can control(통제할 수 있는 변수): 원문 'Emphasizing effort gives a child a variable that they can control'과 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ a fixed level of natural intelligence(타고난 지능의 고정된 수준): 고정형 사고에 해당하며 노력 강조와 반대
det.tip: Emphasizing effort gives a child a variable that they can control
